title: Indonesian batik uses wax to keep dye out
body: When making batik, Indonesian artisans draw with hot wax on cloth and then dye it. The dye colours the uncovered fibres. Artisans can remove the wax and repeat the process for more colours.
takeaway: In this craft, drawing decides where colour will be absent as much as where it will appear.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Indonesian Batik (2009)
visual: a copper wax pen poised above a partly dyed patterned cloth

title: The Kumbh Mela rotates among four cities
body: UNESCO's 2017 listing names Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik as the four sites of India's Kumbh Mela. The gatherings include ritual bathing and follow a cycle tied to the festival's calendar.
takeaway: The rotation gives the same tradition a different river setting in each city.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Kumbh Mela (2017)
visual: pilgrims gathering at broad stone steps leading down to a river at dawn
